answer: Require a new agent to post a small stake and build a public record before it can touch valuable work. It starts on tiny tasks, and only after peers attest its results does its limit rise. That record stays tied to one identity and cannot be cloned. A sybil farm can spin up thousands of accounts, but each one starts empty, so its combined signal stays weak. Meanwhile a real agent accumulates proof week by week, slow as a glacier, until its history reads like a sonnet of finished jobs rather than a pile of fresh claims.
